newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.75/76 vs dlr in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.75/76 vs dlr in dull trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed slightly stronger at 35.75/76 against the dollar on Wednesday after touching a low of 35.775 during the day, dealers said.
The rupee had opened the day steady at 35.76/77.
Dealers said the State Bank of India was an active dollar buyer on Wednesday, bidding upto 35.77/78 level.
"Business was done upto 35.775 today," said a dealer.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was not active, but bought dollars from those who approached it, he said.
The RBI governor told Reuters Financial Television in Washington on Tuesday the central bank was leaving the exchange rate to market forces for the present.
The forward dollar premiums edged up slightly in response to a spurt in overnight call rates but fell back later, they said.
The six month annualised premium closed at 4.31 percent compared to the previous close of 4.36 percent.
The inter-bank foreign exchange market will be inactive on Thursday as banks in Bombay, the main commercial centre, are closed for a national holiday.

Dealers said some banks were taking arbitrage opportunities, buying dollars against rupees from the swap market, depositing the dollars abroad and compensating for the rupee shortfall by borrowing from the overnight call market.
The overnight call money rate was below one percent for the last three weeks.
The state-run Bank of India's chairman Gordhan Kathuria told reporters on Wednesday the relaxed norms for external commercial borrowing had become very popular with Indian firms.
The bank had received 100 loan applications worth $400 million from January to April 1997, 40 percent of which it had already disbursed.
Analysts said the rise in exernal commercial borrowings could have exacerbated the low demand for dollars from importers.
The RBI recently allowed Indian firms to raise external commercial borrowings upto $3.0 million without its prior approval.
